builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
summary: The method replaces unstructured expert-level pruning or full-model retention in Mixture-of-Experts models by identifying and retaining domain-specialized neurons across expert boundaries using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling. It requires mixed-domain calibration data and preprocessing to compute neuron importance scores, adding implementation complexity compared to magnitude-based pruning. Performance may degrade significantly on out-of-distribution tasks if calibration data does not match production traffic, as neuron specialization was validated on specific academic benchmarks.
rationale: This technique directly addresses the 24GB memory constraint by enabling smaller resident model footprints with documented throughput gains, but requires domain-specific validation before production deployment.

claims.statement: The method replaces unstructured expert-level pruning or full-model retention in Mixture-of-Experts models by identifying and retaining domain-specialized neurons across expert boundaries using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling. It requires mixed-domain calibration data and preprocessing to compute neuron importance scores, adding implementation complexity compared to magnitude-based pruning. Performance may degrade significantly on out-of-distribution tasks if calibration data does not match production traffic, as neuron specialization was validated on specific academic benchmarks.
At 50% retention, RAMPr reduces resident GPU memory by 36-43% and improves batched prefill throughput by 17-39%, preserving 91-98% performance at 75% retention.
